title: Is the Necronomicon real?
summary: Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant are joined by Jonathan Strickland to discuss the Necronomicon, the fictional grimoire created by H.P. Lovecraft, and its place in the Cthulhu mythos. They cover Cthulhu's pronunciation and description, the 'bloop' sound detected in the ocean, the fictional author Abdul Alhazred, real and invented books cited in Lovecraft's stories (Elias Warmius, John Dee), the Necronomicon's afterlife in fan fiction, cults, and pop culture (Evil Dead, Simpsons, Friday the 13th Part IX, Cloverfield). The episode ends with a listener mail from Vic in Lincolnshire, Illinois, about his father's death after a nurse plugged an electric shaver into the outlet for a temporary pacemaker in 1970.

segments.title: Opening banter and introduction of Jonathan Strickland
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck introduce the episode on the Necronomicon and Lovecraft, joke about Lovecraft fans, and introduce guest Jonathan Strickland, who wrote the HowStuffWorks articles on Cthulhu and the Necronomicon.

segments.title: Cthulhu's pronunciation and appearance
segments.summary: The hosts discuss how Lovecraft's creatures have an unpronounceable language, the common pronunciation 'Cthulhu,' and descriptions of Cthulhu with wings, octopus and dragon features, which Lovecraft called unnamable.

segments.title: Cthulhu's role in the Mythos and the bloop
segments.summary: Cthulhu became the central figure of the Lovecraft mythos largely through fans, appearing in only a couple of stories and described as a priest figure for the Old Ones. His sunken city is said to lie off South America, linking to the 'bloop' underwater sound, which marine biologists could not attribute to a whale. The Cloverfield viral marketing tied into speculation about the bloop.
